## Detailed notes

Page facts: by Tal Blevins; URL dated 21 November 2002, page shows "Updated: Nov 24, 2018"; subtitle "A neat little twist on the squad-based puzzle strategy genre."; score 8.2, "great". Metacritic lists it at 82. Commercial review, so paraphrased.

- Context: Spellbound's Desperados (previous year) was a critical hit; this is a brain-teasing action/strategy game on the Robin Hood legend.
- Story: Robin returns from the Crusades to find Prince John has taken his land and displaced Richard, imprisoned in Austria; Robin robs John's men to raise the ransom. The reviewer finds the storyline true to the legend.
- Abilities cited: blocking arrows, throwing an apple to distract, healing with herbs; Robin tossing a purse to make sentries fight; Will Scarlet operating siege weapons (as the review claims); Friar Tuck knocking guards out bloodlessly with his staff.
- Open-ended missions: usually a choice of several missions of varying difficulty (a trained army versus rookies guarding a gold caravan); harder missions pay more, easier ones rest the band.
- Resource management: men left in Sherwood rest, train melee or bow, and produce arrows, purses, nets and herbs; items are finite so allocation matters.
- Objectives vary; direct sword fights are much more viable than in Commandos or Desperados, but too much direct action lowers reputation and recruitment. Macro "quick actions" as in Desperados.
- Complaints: the view keeps scrolling briefly after the cursor leaves the edge, spoiling precise plans; only one enemy's line of sight visible at a time (no Commandos-style "see all"), possibly a deliberate difficulty choice.
- Levels: small forest ambush maps up to the cities of Nottingham, Leicester, Derby, York and Lincoln; 2D backdrops and sprites pixelate at maximum zoom.
- Audio: period-appropriate soundtrack; over-the-top voice acting the reviewer enjoys; sound problems on two Sound Blaster Audigy machines (pauses on voice samples on one, stuttering speech on the other).
- Performance: box minimum PII 233 MHz, reviewer recommends 800 MHz for 1024×768, which he considers indispensable for the wider view.
- Verdict: resource management and non-linear missions are great additions that future genre titles should keep.
